kpis: Instagram at about 800 a week reaches roughly 89K by 31 Dec, so 88K is a safe floor. TikTok passes 10K in early December at current pace, so the stretch target is 15K by March. The booking measures matter most and have no baseline yet; set one from the first two weeks of tracked links.
paid: Paid reach is not bad in itself. The problem is that we can’t tell what it buys. Ask Performance for X Ads and Google Ads data for 30 Sep, 4 Oct, 19 Oct and the August YouTube films: spend, clicks, cost per click and any bookings. Then put a paid flag and spend column in the tracker so paid and organic are never mixed again.
basis: Each source covers a gap in the others. The tracker gives the time series and peers. The 6 Nov analysis gives post-level X reach and the content read. My register adds TikTok post metrics, Snapchat and the full YouTube history, which the tracker cannot see. None of this replaces native analytics: reach, clicks and spend are still unknown.
progress: Progress is real on everything Marketing controls day to day: cadence, TikTok and now booking links. The tracker’s 20 Nov pass verified all 27 follower counts on native pages, but the 53 new X posts have no post-level screenshots. The open items all need someone to hand over data: ad spend, native analytics and visit data. Those are the asks for this meeting.
plan: Detail. 1: UTM per post and per site; booking first in every bio (Instagram led with the App Store). 2: X Ads and Google Ads for the 4 Oct X card and the August YouTube films. 3: character and trend formats proved out (25.1K-view loop); keep a question or tag prompt in each caption. 4: copy the Qiddiya City parks’ 50%-off, link-in-bio format, with a code. 5: Abha has a fixed weekly slot on TikTok but not on Snapchat. 6: retire one of EntertainKSA or SaudiSEVEN on Facebook, fix the YouTube LinkedIn link, one spelling per destination tag. 7: end screens and a subscribe prompt on the ad-served films. 8: test linked film posts against question posts. Actions 1 and 2 matter most: together they let social be judged on bookings rather than views.
content: The tone is Arabic-first, in Saudi dialect, and consistently on the “Joy” idea. The calendar has followed Tabuk’s Hot Wheels launch. TikTok has started to give Abha a regular slot; Snapchat has not. Captions rarely give a reason to visit now: no price, offer, new attraction or date, except the blood-donation gifts.
peers: The two Qiddiya City parks are the most useful benchmark: same parent, similar Instagram size, much larger TikTok and much higher X reach per follower, helped by smaller X audiences. Their offer posts (50% off, link in bio) are a model for SEVEN’s coded offers.
hygiene: None of this costs money to fix. One bio line, one Facebook page, a fixed LinkedIn link and a hashtag style sheet (no punctuation inside tags, one spelling per destination) should be done within two weeks. YouTube needs a decision: either a real Shorts cadence fed by TikTok cuts, or treat it as an ad library and stop counting its views as organic.
scene: Scene is in scope because SEVEN owns the brand. Volume isn’t the problem; Scene posts more than SEVEN. Conversion intent is. A linked film post is the cheapest test in this deck.
tiktok-growth: The first five weeks added about 200 followers a week. From 29 Oct to 19 Nov SEVEN added 3,473 in three weeks. The 6 Nov analysis had TikTok behind its 475-a-week plan; it is now well ahead. Set a more ambitious target (15K by end of March is proposed later) so the team keeps pushing.
footprint: Instagram is where SEVEN’s audience lives, roughly nine times TikTok and fifty times YouTube. TikTok is the growth story. X has stopped growing for every account in the tracker, not just SEVEN. YouTube and Snapchat are not in the tracker; they come from my capture.
ig-x: Instagram is compounding: weekly gains went from +300 to +900, and the last two weeks averaged about +800 (the 12 Nov reading was missing, so we have only the two-week total of +1,600). X follower counts have not moved for anyone in the tracker. SEVEN’s typical X post still reaches 3–4% of followers, above the 3% target and above every cinema and mall.
booking: This is the clearest sign of progress since 6 Nov: the recommendation to add booking links is being applied on X. Next, bring it to Instagram and TikTok, where the audience is larger, and tag each link per post and per site (UTM), so social can be tied to bookings. VOX shows what full coverage looks like.
gaps: Close by agreeing owners and dates for the three handovers. With them, the next assessment can report cost per booking by channel and site, instead of public views. Ask the meeting to confirm the proposed targets and the 90-day plan owners.
engagement: X interactions are replies, reposts, likes and bookmarks. On Instagram only likes are public, and they depend on post age. TikTok gives the richest signal and the highest response, so it should get the creative experiments. Read the 17 Nov X post closely: we don’t know if it was boosted, but its engagement ratio is far above the 4 Oct ad-scale post.
cover: Purpose: one view of where SEVEN stands on social, built from three inputs: the 9-week weekly tracker (27 account rows, verified on 20 Nov), the 6 Nov analysis and its evidence packs, and a fresh capture of 71 SEVEN posts with screenshots taken 19–20 Nov. The headline: audience momentum is real, especially TikTok, and the booking link has started to appear. The work now is to make every post bookable and measurable, and to settle what paid spend is buying.
summary: Four numbers carry the story. Audience: TikTok more than doubled in eight weeks and Instagram added 4.5K followers. Booking path: the first booking links appeared on X this week, a direct response to the 6 Nov recommendation, but they are not yet on every post or platform. Paid reach: the largest view counts SEVEN shows, on X and YouTube, come with almost no reactions, which points to paid distribution that we cannot yet judge on bookings.
tiktok-posts: The breakout is a trend-native loop of a dancing character, with no venue footage. It drew 25.1K views and 53 shares; its 1.0% engagement rate is lower because it reached people beyond SEVEN’s followers. The posts with the most comments ask a question or ask people to tag friends. Straight venue promos sit around 1.5–2.5K views. Brief more character and trend content, and keep a question in every caption.
